title: Archive and Signal Again
premise: Elodie Hartwell smuggles forbidden memories through orbital customs while quietly maintaining a beacon that predates the colony itself. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams—memories of Earth's final days that no one alive should possess—Elodie traces the signal to the beacon and discovers it's been broadcasting to the cryosleep vaults, where two half-populations wait for contradictory wake orders: one loyal to the colony's founders, one carrying proof of their crimes. The beacon demands she choose which half wakes. In the end, Elodie refuses both options, rewrites the beacon's code with her own smuggled memories as the tiebreaker, and forces the sleeping generations to wake together into a truth neither faction wanted.
about_author: Elodie Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent seven years maintaining remote listening stations in the Atacama Desert before turning to fiction. Her work explores what machines remember when humans choose to forget.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A routine smuggling run past orbital customs introduces her world: memory-chips sewn into coat linings, bribed inspectors, the loneliness of invisibility. She returns to maintain the ancient beacon, her private ritual. Emotional beat: competent isolation—the comfort and cost of being no one.

chapters.title: The Children's Chorus
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Colony children recite identical dreams at school: burning skies, a sealed door, a woman's voice counting down. Officials dismiss it as a fad; Elodie recognizes the countdown cadence—it matches the beacon's transmission rhythm. Emotional beat: dread blooming beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. She decrypts the beacon's core and finds it's not a navigation aid but a relay, forwarding pre-collapse Earth archives into the cryovaults' dream-state systems. Someone programmed it to prepare sleepers for waking. Emotional beat: vertigo—her sanctuary was always a weapon.

chapters.title: Two Halves of Tomorrow
chapters.summary: POV Elodie, with flashbacks from founder Ilsa Voss's stored memories. The beacon holds two wake protocols: Vault A carries the founders' sanitized history; Vault B carries evidence they sabotaged Earth's evacuation to seize power. Each protocol excludes the other half of humanity. Emotional beat: horror at the arithmetic of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Customs chief Adeyemi, her oldest ally, reveals he's known about her beacon maintenance for years—he's been protecting her because his own daughter sleeps in Vault B. He asks her to trigger B's protocol. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized by love.

chapters.title: Signal Bleed
chapters.summary: POV alternating Elodie and ten-year-old Mira, a dreamer child. The children's shared dreams intensify as the beacon's signal strengthens; Mira begins waking with full memories of Earth's last day. Colony authorities trace the anomaly toward Elodie's district. Emotional beat: innocence conscripted into an adult war.

chapters.title: The Countdown She Chose
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Cornered by authorities and Voss's descendants, Elodie learns the beacon will auto-execute Protocol A in nine days unless overridden by an authorized memory-key—which only a registered founder can provide. Adeyemi offers a forged key; it will fail and expose them all. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Everything I Ever Carried
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. She realizes her smuggling career was the answer: decades of contraband memories—unfiltered, unaligned with either faction—form a third archive. She begins splicing them into the beacon, knowing the process will burn out her own memory implants. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Wake Order
chapters.summary: POV Elodie and Mira. Climax: authorities storm the beacon station as the countdown hits zero. Elodie executes her rewritten protocol—both vaults wake simultaneously, flooded with her contraband archive so no faction controls the narrative. She loses most of her own memories mid-broadcast. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with self-erasure.

chapters.title: Archive and Signal
chapters.summary: POV Mira, years later. The unified colony struggles but endures; children still dream, but now the dreams are theirs alone. Mira maintains the beacon and reads to a memory-fragmented Elodie, returning to her the story of what she did. Emotional beat: memory survives not in machines but in the people who carry it forward.
